correctness.rationale: The exact prime-factor identity Delta_k(n)=sum_{p^a||n}(gcd(k,a)-log_2(a+1)) settles all cases. For k=1 every summand is nonpositive and is zero exactly when a=1; prime powers q^a give Delta→−infinity. For k>=2 choose any prime divisor r of k and let N_t be a product of t distinct primes each to exponent r: Delta_k(N_t)=t[r-log_2(r+1)]→+infinity because 2^r>r+1. Conversely M_t=q^{kt+1} has gcd(k,kt+1)=1 and Delta_k(M_t)=1-log_2(kt+2)→−infinity. These constructions prove an infinite global range rather than merely finite examples. Independent finite exponent-regression checks support the algebra without claiming to prove the limits.
